content: A person doesn't die when he should, but when he can.
author: Gabriel García Márquez
sourceWork: Gabriel García Márquez's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

In Gabriel García Márquez's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
